title: Food chain cards: woodland, pond and sea
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Properties of materials and habitats (Alchemy Island and Living Things and Their Habitats)
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 17 (Food chain cards: woodland, pond and sea (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 17: Food chains: producers and consumers. To understand that food chains show how energy passes from producers to consumers

questions.q: Write a food chain: lettuce, slug, thrush.
questions.model: Start with the producer: lettuce. What eats it? Slug. What eats the slug? Thrush. Arrows point to the eater: lettuce → slug → thrush.

questions.q: In that chain, which is the predator?

questions.a: 'Is eaten by': energy passes along it.

questions.q: Core: Write three food chains from a woodland, a pond and the sea. Label producer, prey and predator.
questions.a: For example: acorn → squirrel → fox; pondweed → tadpole → heron; seaweed → limpet → crab.
questions.model: Teacher writes the first: oak leaf → caterpillar → blue tit. Producer: oak leaf. Prey: caterpillar. Predator: blue tit.

questions.q: Extend: In grass → rabbit → fox, what happens if the rabbits disappear?
questions.a: Foxes have less food and may decrease; grass may grow more.

questions.q: Stretch: Why are there usually fewer predators than prey?
questions.a: Energy is used up at each step, so less is passed on to the predators.

questions.q: Every food chain starts with a...
Big question: where does the energy in a fox's dinner really come from?
questions.a: From the Sun, through the grass and then the rabbit.
